To be honest, this course has been a real letdown for me. While I understand the importance of learning about translation methodology, the way it’s been taught just hasn’t clicked with me. The content often felt repetitive, and a lot of the terms and theories seemed irrelevant or too niche to actually be useful in a professional setting. It felt like we were focusing more on memorizing obscure terminology than on gaining practical skills or insights that would help us in the real world.

The slides we used throughout the semester didn’t help much either. They were dense with information but lacked focus and clear direction. Topics like "queer translation" and "eco-translation", for example, felt especially far-fetched—almost as if they were included just to fill up the curriculum. While these might have some academic value, they seemed disconnected from the kind of challenges we’ll face as professional translators. I kept wondering why we were spending so much time on these niche areas when there are far more relevant and practical aspects of translation that could’ve been emphasized.

And then there’s the exam format. It felt more like a test of memorization skills than an opportunity to engage critically with the material. If the goal was for us to critique translated texts or apply methodologies, wouldn’t it make more sense to allow a cheat sheet or some kind of reference material? That’s how real-life translation works—you consult resources to ensure the best outcome. Instead, the exams just felt like a memorization challenge, which doesn’t align with what we actually need to learn.Overall, the course came across as something designed to tick off a box in the curriculum rather than provide meaningful preparation for our careers.
